subject: SIG questionnaire + DPA / SCCs / HIPAA feasibility for MediSync
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@medisync.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Baker <tom.baker@medisync.com>
Date: 2026-10-29T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Vendor SIG + privacy questions (MediSync)

Hi Jonas —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement ran a quick intake and attached is our standard vendor compliance request (see vendor-compliance-request.pdf). We need the following to proceed:

- Completed SIG questionnaire (we prefer the current SIG v2025 template)
- Copy of your latest SOC 2 report
- Confirmation you can sign our DPA / accept SCCs for EU data transfers
- Clarify whether Redwood can support HIPAA/BAA for a partner integration (we host PHI in some EU regions)

Can you confirm an estimated turnaround and whether any of this would require special contracting or a private/on-prem deployment?

Thanks —
Elena Ruiz
Head of Vendor Risk, MediSync Health

Attachments: vendor-compliance-request.pdf (pdf)

On Thu, Oct 29, 2026 at 11:02 AM Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com> wrote:
> Elena —
> 
> Appreciate the packet. Quick plan from our side:
> ...

Thanks Jonas — looping in a few details from security's side.

Elena, to make sure we return a useful SIG: can you confirm whether MediSync expects:
- SCCs (EU Commission Standard Contractual Clauses) to be applied to cross-border transfers? If so, which set (controller-controller vs controller-processor)?
- Any additional regional controls (e.g., data residency in the EU required for EU patients)?

Practical notes:
- We will attach our SOC 2 Type II report (current as of 2026-05) and our pen test summary.
- Evidence pull: our compliance repo includes policy docs, diagrams, and sample config exports — we will provide redacted artifacts.
- SIG completion ETA: draft answer sheet by 2026-11-02.

If HIPAA/BAA is in scope, we need to confirm the data flows (what types of PHI, retention, who initiates de-identification). A BAA often requires additional contractual terms and operational controls (audit logging, per-tenant encryption keys). We can support BAA in Dedicated/Private setups more readily; hosted can be considered with specific controls and contractual language.

Marissa Cole
Head of Security, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachments referenced: redwood-soc2-report-202605.pdf (will provide), pen-test-summary-202605.pdf (will provide)

From: Elena Ruiz <elena@medisync.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Baker <tom.baker@medisync.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Vendor SIG + privacy questions (MediSync)

Thanks — quick clarifications:

- Yes, we require controller-processor SCCs (Annex I in our template).
- EU data residency is required for our EU patient data subsets (we host EU patients in eu-west-1).
- HIPAA: we are a digital therapeutics partner and will be sending limited PHI (identifiers + health status). We require a BAA or equivalent; can Redwood sign a BAA? If not, what are alternative mitigations (encryption, tokenization, private deployment)?

I've added our procurement link: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/12345 — your procurement contact is Tom Baker. We can be flexible with timeline but would like a response on HIPAA feasibility within this week if possible.

Elena

Quoted attachment: vendor-compliance-request.pdf

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@medisync.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Vendor SIG + privacy questions (MediSync)

Elena / Tom —

Thanks for the clear asks. A few concrete items from Legal:

- DPA / SCCs: we can accept the standard controller-processor SCCs with a limited set of negotiated terms. I'll prepare a DPA draft (using our template) and mark any clauses where we typically request alternate language. Expect a redline within 3 business days.
- SOC 2: Marissa will attach our 2026 Type II report; we can provide an NDA'd copy if needed.
- HIPAA / BAA: high level — Redwood can consider a BAA but we need:
  a) an architecture diagram showing where PHI will traverse / be stored;
  b) an agreement on data residency (EU region pinning); and
  c) confirmation that MediSync's use case is limited to covered functions requiring a BAA.

Operationally, options are: hosted + contractual BAA with scoped controls (might require additional logging and KMS configuration), or Dedicated/Private deployment which is simpler from an operational separation perspective and aligns well with BAA obligations. If you need a BAA, please confirm whether MediSync will accept a Dedicated environment or requires hosted.

Next steps I propose:
1) Jonas — deliver completed SIG draft and attach SOC2 + pen test artifacts (by EOD 2026-11-02).
2) Marissa — provide the SOC2 + evidence links.
3) Me (Legal) — send initial DPA redline; schedule procurement-friendly timeline with Tom.
4) If BAA needed, schedule a short architecture call (30 min) this week so engineering can scope changes.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
